segments.t: A fresh korTTY window: the customizable icon toolbar, the terminal area (where session tabs and the optional dashboard appear once you connect), and the status bar. The following diagram maps the same regions:
korTTY's main window has these regions:

KTPH000Icon toolbarKTPH001 — direct actions grouped into Terminal, Tools and Settings above the menu bar, with a separate row for your saved server and group buttons. See KTPH002Customizing the icon toolbarKTPH003.

KTPH012Menu barKTPH013 — visible by default in each new window. Right-click either icon-toolbar row and choose KTPH014Show/hide menu barKTPH015 to show or hide it for this window; its check mark reflects the current state. You can also use KTPH016KTPH000KTPH017+KTPH018KTPH001KTPH019+KTPH020KTPH002KTPH021 (KTPH022KTPH003KTPH023+KTPH024KTPH004KTPH025+KTPH026KTPH005KTPH027 on macOS). Visibility is a session choice and is not saved. The macOS system menu bar remains available. The in-window menus are File · Edit · Connections · Configuration · Tools · AI · Teamwork · Plugins · View · Help. All features are reachable here and via KTPH028keyboard shortcutsKTPH029, and the KTPH030command paletteKTPH031 (KTPH032KTPH006KTPH033+KTPH034KTPH007KTPH035+KTPH036KTPH008KTPH037, KTPH038KTPH009KTPH039+KTPH040KTPH010KTPH041+KTPH042KTPH011KTPH043 on macOS) finds and runs any menu command by name, also while the menu bar is hidden, runs the terminal's right-click commands such as KTPH044Clear BufferKTPH045, switches to any open tab, the ones you used last first, connects to any saved connection and runs any snippet in the terminal. A live KTPH046JobScheduler statusKTPH047 menu appears after KTPH048HelpKTPH049 when a scheduled entry is active. While a KTPH050guide translationKTPH051 runs, a progress indicator (bar, percentage and estimated time remaining) sits at the right end of the menu-bar row and stays visible even when the menu bar itself is hidden.

KTPH014Tab barKTPH015 — each SSH/Mosh session runs in its own tab, named after its connection, or after the KTPH016title its shell setsKTPH017 or a name you give it with KTPH018Rename TabKTPH019. KTPH020KTPH000KTPH021+KTPH022KTPH001KTPH023 opens Quick Connect for a new tab; KTPH024KTPH002KTPH025+KTPH026KTPH003KTPH027 / KTPH028KTPH004KTPH029+KTPH030KTPH005KTPH031+KTPH032KTPH006KTPH033 switch tabs, in tab bar order or, if you switch it on in the KTPH034Window settingsKTPH035, in the order you last used them, and KTPH036KTPH007KTPH037+KTPH038KTPH008KTPH039 to KTPH040KTPH009KTPH041+KTPH042KTPH010KTPH043 jump to the first to eighth tab and KTPH044KTPH011KTPH045+KTPH046KTPH012KTPH047 to the last one (KTPH048KTPH013KTPH049 on macOS). A colored dot in front of a tab's title, and a frame of the same color around its terminal, show the KTPH050tab colorKTPH051 of its connection, or of its credential's KTPH052environmentKTPH053; the frame can be switched off in the KTPH054Window settingsKTPH055. An amber fork icon after it marks a tab whose typing goes to other panes, through KTPH056multi-execKTPH057 or KTPH058broadcast modeKTPH059; its tooltip says which. With KTPH060Open tool windows as tabsKTPH061 enabled (KTPH062Window settingsKTPH063), management tools such as Snippets, the JobScheduler or the AI Manager open here as tabs too — in the window whose menu you used — instead of as separate windows. The KTPH064Snippet ManagerKTPH065 keeps the snippets you edit as tabs of its own inside its tab.

KTPH003DashboardKTPH004 (toggle KTPH005KTPH000KTPH006+KTPH007KTPH001KTPH008+KTPH009KTPH002KTPH010) — a side panel listing every open connection with status dots, protocol badges and AI-agent badges. See KTPH011DashboardKTPH012 below.

KTPH000File browserKTPH001 (KTPH002View → File Browser ▸ Show on Left / Show on RightKTPH003) — a dockable local file manager with navigation toolbar, path bar, filter, type icons and a folder/file/selection counter. Its side, width, hidden-file state and last directory are restored on the next launch. See KTPH004File browserKTPH005.

KTPH003Live journal panelKTPH004 (KTPH005View → Live JournalKTPH006, KTPH007KTPH000KTPH008+KTPH009KTPH001KTPH010+KTPH011KTPH002KTPH012) — the active tab's running KTPH013session journalKTPH014 as its full journal page, docked and updating in real time; side and width are restored on the next launch.

KTPH003Coding Agents panelKTPH004 (KTPH005View → Coding AgentsKTPH006, KTPH007KTPH000KTPH008+KTPH009KTPH001KTPH010+KTPH011KTPH002KTPH012) — docks beside the terminal area on the left or right and lists every coding agent detected in any korTTY window. It shows and hides itself with agent detection unless KTPH013Automatically show and hide the coding-agent sidebarKTPH014 is switched off, and it keeps its last side and width. See KTPH015Coding agentsKTPH016.
KTPH000Terminal areaKTPH001 — the active terminal, with optional split-screen and broadcast input.

KTPH000Status barKTPH001 — connection state, host/IP, active protocol, temporary SSH-key timer and connection duration. While panes take part in KTPH002multi-execKTPH003, an amber chip in every window counts them, with the tabs and windows they are in, and its KTPH004StopKTPH005 link ends multi-exec everywhere.

Press KTPH006KTPH000KTPH007+KTPH008KTPH001KTPH009+KTPH010KTPH002KTPH011 (or KTPH012View → Terminal-only FullscreenKTPH013) to show the whole korTTY window — menus, tabs and status bar included — kept at its previous window size and centered on an empty fullscreen background, so the desktop and other windows stop competing for attention. KTPH014View → Hide terminal scrollbars in fullscreenKTPH015 removes the scrollbars too. A transparent terminal background becomes opaque while fullscreen is active and returns to its saved level when you leave. Press KTPH016KTPH003KTPH017+KTPH018KTPH004KTPH019+KTPH020KTPH005KTPH021 again to restore.

The icon toolbar is visible by default, including when upgrading a configuration that has no toolbar settings yet. Its original vector icons use theme-colored outlines with small colored details, so they remain recognizable in light and dark designs. KTPH000View → Action toolbarKTPH001 and KTPH002View → Connection toolbarKTPH003 independently show or hide the two rows. The same switches and KTPH004Show/hide menu barKTPH005 are available when you right-click either row. If the menu bar is hidden, right-click the status bar to restore either toolbar. Both visibility preferences and button placement are shared across windows and survive restarts. Older configurations keep their previous visibility for both rows until you change them separately.

The first row groups KTPH000New TabKTPH001 and KTPH002New local shellKTPH003 under Terminal; SFTP, Snippet Manager, Session Journals, Logfile Manager, AI Manager, JobScheduler and Video Manager under Tools; and Font, Colors, Keyboard, Logs, Window, Terminal and AI shortcuts under Settings, in that order. The Global Settings button is available in the customization catalog but is not included in the default layout. KTPH004New TabKTPH005 opens Quick Connect. KTPH006New local shellKTPH007 immediately starts a tab with the existing platform-default shell preset. Tooltips name each action and its current keyboard shortcut, where one exists. Buttons that do not fit remain reachable through the toolbar overflow menu. Set KTPH008Toolbar icon size (px)KTPH009 from 16 to 64 in KTPH010Global Settings → WindowKTPH011; the default is 24, and saving updates both rows and the customization catalog in every window.

When an older saved toolbar layout is loaded for the first time, korTTY automatically adds the Logfile Manager button after Session Journals in Tools, or at the end of Tools if Session Journals is absent. Existing buttons, separators, their order and the visibility of both rows are preserved. A Logfile Manager button you already placed stays where it is, without adding a duplicate. After this migration, removing the button through customization is remembered.

Right-click the toolbar and choose KTPH000Customize toolbar…KTPH001. Both rows appear as editable destinations, including a row you have hidden, and a catalog opens underneath them, filtered by the name you type in its search field, with room for at least two complete button rows, including wrapped labels. Catalog buttons wrap at spaces or hyphens and widen for words that would otherwise be cut off. Finishing or cancelling customization restores each row’s saved visibility. Choose KTPH002ActionsKTPH003, KTPH004SettingsKTPH005 or KTPH006ConnectionsKTPH007 in its category list. Click a catalog button to append it to its default section, or drag it to the desired position. The Settings category offers one shortcut for each main tab of Global Settings. KTPH008Add connectionKTPH009 opens the Connections category, populated from the Connection Manager. KTPH010SeparatorKTPH011 adds a movable divider.

Drag an existing button to move it. Click or right-click it for KTPH006Remove buttonKTPH007, KTPH008Move leftKTPH009, KTPH010Move rightKTPH011 and KTPH012Move to sectionKTPH013. With an editable button focused, KTPH014KTPH000KTPH015+KTPH016KTPH001KTPH017 / KTPH018KTPH002KTPH019+KTPH020KTPH003KTPH021 moves it and KTPH022KTPH004KTPH023 or KTPH024KTPH005KTPH025 removes it. Actions can move among the three task sections; saved server and group buttons stay in the connection row. In this mode, clicking a destination button never starts its action or a connection.

KTPH000FinishKTPH001 saves the edited layout. KTPH002CancelKTPH003 discards it. KTPH004DefaultKTPH005 restores the standard layout in the editing preview, so it can still be cancelled. A deliberately empty configuration stays empty and offers KTPH006Customize toolbar…KTPH007. The connection row is hidden when empty during normal use and always available while customizing.

Server buttons show the saved connection name and connect through the existing sign-in flow. Group buttons show the full group path and open only its direct members, one tab each; they do not include subgroups. Existing policy restrictions remain enforced. As with Quick Connect's group action, password-authenticated group members without a stored password are skipped with a message. Renaming a group in the Connection Manager updates toolbar references. Deleted or unavailable targets remain disabled and can be removed or replaced while customizing. Toolbar settings store references, never copies of passwords or keys.

Toggle the dashboard with KTPH003KTPH000KTPH004+KTPH005KTPH001KTPH006+KTPH007KTPH002KTPH008 or KTPH009View → Show DashboardKTPH010. It slides in on the left, sizes its width to the longest entry, and follows the active App Design's colors.

The header shows the panel title with two buttons: a collapse/expand toggle (collapses everything while any node is open, expands everything otherwise) and a refresh button. Below it, connections are organized as a tree:
KTPH000Main windowKTPH001 — the root node, with an active/total session count.

KTPH000EnvironmentsKTPH001 — connections whose stored credential has an environment (for example KTPH002ProductionKTPH003 or KTPH004TestKTPH005) are clustered under an environment node; connections without one sit directly under the main window.
KTPH000GroupsKTPH001 — tabs assigned to a connection group appear under their group node. Saving a changed group in the Connection Manager updates open tabs immediately.

Each connection row shows a type icon, a status dot, the server name, and a protocol badge (KTPH000, KTPH001 or KTPH002). The status dot distinguishes three states: filled green for a healthy connection, filled red for a connection that dropped unexpectedly (including a Mosh network interruption), and a hollow outline for a session that ended normally. Terminals with AI-agent runs carry the same ✋/⚡/⏸/✓ badge as elsewhere. Hovering a row shows KTPH003 and the connection state; double-click (or KTPH005KTPH004KTPH006) focuses the session's tab.

Right-click a connection for KTPH000FocusKTPH001, KTPH002DuplicateKTPH003, KTPH004ReconnectKTPH005, KTPH006SFTP-Client...KTPH007 (connected sessions only) and KTPH008CloseKTPH009. KTPH010CloseKTPH011 asks first, like the tab's close button, when the session has split panes or a command is still running. KTPH012Multi-exec: Include All Panes of This TabKTPH013 on a connection row, and KTPH014Multi-exec: Include This PaneKTPH015 on the row of one pane of a split tab, let those panes take part in KTPH016multi-execKTPH017 from any window, without switching to them; the check mark shows whether they take part, and an amber fork icon marks their rows. A footer keeps a running "connected of total" count, and an empty panel shows a placeholder until the first session opens.
On macOS, right-click (or Control-click) the korTTY icon in the Dock for quick actions without switching to the app — they apply to the current (focused) window, opening one first if none is open:
See the KTPH000menu referenceKTPH001 for every menu item and the KTPH002keyboard-shortcuts referenceKTPH003 for the full list of accelerators.
